page: Amazon Web Services r6g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro System and provides 16 dedicated physical cores (1 thread per core) clocked at 2.5 GHz. Cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The server includes no GPUs and no bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions, while network performance features a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate balanced multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread capacity. Under stress-ng, the server delivers an average multi-core score of 24,284.19 and an average single-core score of 1,519.50. Geekbench testing reflects this dichotomy, scoring 8,428.0 in multi-core operations (average) versus 929.0 in single-core performance (poor tier). Memory throughput reaches 946.72 GB/sec for small cached reads and 121.62 GB/sec for large uncached reads, while large block write bandwidth achieves 53.38 GB/sec. Parallelized tasks perform reliably, as evidenced by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 61.96 GB/sec and software compilation in Clang reaching 15,358.0 points. In contrast, instruction-constrained tasks like single-threaded bzip3 decompression (6.76 GB/sec) and LLM inference generation on small models (39.7 tokens/sec) fall into lower percentiles due to the absence of advanced vector acceleration extensions such as AVX or AMX.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6g.4xlarge leverages custom ARM silicon to provide a high RAM-per-core density without the pricing premium often associated with x86 memory-heavy instances. Because each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical core without simultaneous multithreading, computational latency remains stable across concurrent memory operations. These hardware parameters make the instance suitable for distributed in-memory caching systems, intermediate database tiers, data aggregation workloads, and high-concurrency web services that rely on large active memory pools rather than single-threaded clock speed.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz and 128.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core). Driven by AWS Graviton silicon on the Nitro hypervisor, the server does not include local storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmarks, the instance yields average multi-core efficiency, logging 24,284.19 in stress-ng and 8,428.0 in Geekbench multi-core, while single-thread results rank in lower tiers. Memory bandwidth reaches 121.62 GB/sec on large reads and Redis throughput scales to 18.82 million operations per second. The server offers cost-effective memory density without x86 overhead, making it well fitted for in-memory databases, Redis caches, mid-tier data processing, and scalable backend services.
